Commentary.Commentary: Afghanistan were poor with the ball. The spinners got enough purchase but were not consistent enough to build some pressure. Afghanistan got tired as the game progressed, Bangladesh were  in no mood to milk them for runs while Afghanistan couldn't help themselves but to keep the spirit up and keep bowling. A massive task awaits for them. Afghanistan need 662 runs to win. Feels like a lot will happen in the next couple of hours.

The declaration has finally come. So, Bangladesh have declared with a massive lead of 661 runs. A tough task awaits for Afghanistan who have been chasing this game right from the start. Even the cracks have started to open up which doesn't help the visitors as it will get difficult to bat on. Bangladesh have been outstanding with the bat. Shanto was the hero for them with back-to-back centuries. Mominul Haque then got to his century while the skipper got his fifty. Najmul Hossain Shanto though played a big part in this massive lead. Bangladesh certain to win here.

Hello and welcome everyone to the action of Day 3. Bangladesh have a massive lead already but they would probably like to add a 100 runs more before going all-in with the ball. Afghanistan are well behind in this game. Before looking at the final target, they have to take wickets as quickly as possible and hope Bangladesh do not score freely in the first session. Stay tuned for more updates.
...Day 3, Session1...

Bangladesh didn't enforce the follow-on though, a good idea as that allowed their bowlers to charge up and go full throttle on Day 3 with a hefty lead now. Afghanistan need a miracle, we feel Bangladesh will look for a score around 400. Do join us back on Day 3 at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) and earlier for the build up. Cheers!

Bangladesh are in a very comfortable position as they now lead by 367 runs. Looks more than enough with the quality bowls they have. Bangladesh started Day 3 with the bat, having 5 wickets in hand but Afghanistan bowled well, Nijat Masood in particular as he took the remaining wickets quickly. However, their batters didn't replicate the same effort as they were put under pressure right from the start by the Bangladeshi seamers. Afghanistan kept on losing wickets and not a single batter scored more than 40.
